reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, the full CoverageEligibilityRequest StructureDefinition report, the deterministic aggregate prepass, and the shared behavior context. I also checked the R4 and R6 StructureDefinition element definitions for `provider`, `statusReason`, `event`, and `serviced[x]` directly in the local core packages. Direct behavior findings for CoverageEligibilityRequest were absent; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 CoverageEligibilityRequest is trial-use/FMM 2, so the baseline stability pressure is neutral. That lowers the burden compared with mature or normative resources, but it does not erase business-risk concerns in financial eligibility workflows, especially where unchanged wire shape can hide a changed provider-role interpretation.

overall.oneLineConclusion: CoverageEligibilityRequest is structurally stable from R4 to R6; no broad resource migration program is forced, but the `provider` semantic wording still deserves per-change compatibility review.

reasoning.thesisMd: CoverageEligibilityRequest keeps the same canonical identity and the common local model remains largely intact: no local element was removed or renamed, common cardinalities/types/reference targets are stable, required `status` and `purpose` codes remain compatible in the packaged code systems, and there are no direct behavior findings. The actual migration shape is therefore not a resource redesign. The meaningful work is local: preserving or mapping R6-only optional data and reviewing one hidden semantic shift in `provider`.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: Existing R4 instances should generally migrate forward without a resource-level transformation beyond normal version metadata/validator changes. R6 adds optional `statusReason` and optional repeatable `event`; their required children apply only when new R6 `event` content is present. Those additions create R6-to-R4 downgrade and mixed-version exchange chores, not an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 instance break. The `provider` element keeps its path, cardinality, type, target profiles, definition, and requirements, but the comment changes the business framing from request responsibility/requestor toward billing-provider/data-accountability language.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because no broad migration program is already unavoidable, compatibility leverage remains high at the individual-change level. This is not a case where a major remodel makes local preservation unimportant. Low-cost compatibility-preserving wording for `provider` is still valuable, while optional R6 additions should be handled with conversion guidance rather than used as evidence of a resource-level break.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The clearest less-breaking opportunity is the `provider` comment: R6 could explicitly preserve the R4 request-responsibility meaning and add non-exclusive billing-provider/accountability guidance, or separate the billing-provider concept if it is intended to be distinct. That is low model cost because the computable element shape did not change. For `statusReason` and `event`, the better mitigations are official extensions, ConceptMaps, or StructureMaps for R6-to-R4 exchange; those are useful migration aids, but not required to make the base R6 resource backward-compatible for existing R4 instances.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: There are no direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior findings whose affected resources include CoverageEligibilityRequest as a resource-specific surface. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings may matter to generic servers, clients, validators, and conformance tooling, but under this review they do not make CoverageEligibilityRequest itself a resource-level migration program.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's main conclusion: `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = No`, migration shape `low-material-change`, and compatibility posture `preserve-compatibility-per-change`. The important nuance is that the aggregate's low resource-level migration burden should not down-rank the `provider` Revisit finding; because the resource is otherwise stable, that low-cost semantic compatibility issue has more, not less, review value.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural conclusion because the package StructureDefinitions directly confirm the element shapes. Confidence is lower for the intended business semantics of `provider` because no official narrative change note or ballot rationale was available locally, and the R6 comment uses claim-oriented wording inside CoverageEligibilityRequest.

findingConsiderations.title: Provider comment shifts from request responsibility toward billing-provider/data-accountability semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most important local compatibility concern. It does not force a structural migration, but it can silently change payer routing, accountability, audit, or UI semantics because the same `provider` reference remains syntactically valid while the R6 comment calls it the Billing Provider and refers to claim data accountability. Since a wording-only alternative could preserve the R4 requestor/request-responsibility interpretation, this remains standards-review-worthy despite the otherwise low resource-level migration burden.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds repeatable CoverageEligibilityRequest.event backbone with mandatory children when present
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The new `event` backbone is optional, so it does not invalidate R4 instances and does not make resource-wide migration unavoidable. It still matters for mixed-version exchange because repeatable typed events cannot be losslessly collapsed into R4 `serviced[x]`; implementers need a conversion or extension policy for R6 event-bearing instances.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional summary element CoverageEligibilityRequest.statusReason
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This optional R6 addition is forward-compatible for R4 data and is not evidence of a resource-level migration program. It should be handled as a local R6-to-R4 preservation chore where status-change reasons are operationally or audit relevant.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real shared Resource operation concern, but CoverageEligibilityRequest is neither Resource nor DomainResource for purposes of this resource-level adjudication. It may affect generic validation workflows around CoverageEligibilityRequest instances, yet it should be resolved in the shared operation review rather than treated as a CoverageEligibilityRequest model migration driver.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit `CoverageEligibilityRequest.provider` wording before finalizing R6: preserve the R4 request-responsibility/requestor meaning explicitly, and add billing-provider/data-accountability guidance as non-exclusive text or as a distinct/profiled role if materially different.

Publish or adopt conversion guidance for R6-only `event` and `statusReason` when exchanging with R4 systems, preferably with standard extensions or StructureMap/ConceptMap rules that avoid silent data loss.

Do not plan a broad CoverageEligibilityRequest resource migration solely from the R6 base StructureDefinition changes; focus migration testing on the provider semantic interpretation and R6-to-R4 downgrade examples.

caveats: No official R4-to-R6 CoverageEligibilityRequest narrative diff, change proposal, or ballot rationale was available locally.
No official cross-version CoverageEligibilityRequest ConceptMap or StructureMap was available for the R6-only optional elements.
The R6 input package is 6.0.0-ballot4, so details may change before final publication.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered as context only and were not scored as direct CoverageEligibilityRequest behavior changes.
